sources.notes:
HOW IT WAS READ (no guessing, nothing inferred): a plain fetch of the article does return only loading.gif placeholders in the rendered DOM, exactly as warned. However, the served HTML embeds a schema.org NewsArticle JSON-LD block whose "articleBody" field contains the complete article markup, and every lazy card widget carries its payload in a data-name attribute (e.g. data-name="3 Quantum Riddler || 1 Cruelclaw's Heist || ..."). That is the same string the widget renders from, so the quantities and names below are the article's own text, not OCR of images and not reconstruction from card art. Two attempts to open a real browser were made first (preview_start timed out after 300s), so this static route was used instead; it yielded strictly more reliable data than image alt-text would have.

COMPLETENESS CHECK: the page contains exactly 23 "Loading icon" widgets. Accounted for: 1 decklist loader (deck-364116), 8 deck-tech illustration widgets in the Maindeck/Sideboard commentary, and 14 sideboard-guide widgets = 7 matchups x (IN + OUT). All 7 matchups named in the task rendered and are reported; none are missing or omitted. Section order in the guide is: Dimir Excruciator (the mirror), Temur Harmonizer, Izzet Lessons, Mono Red Aggro, Four-Color Rhythm, Jeskai Control, Bant Airbending.

THE 75: the article's decklist widget is an embed of Cardsrealm deck #364116. That deck page also lazy-loads, but its HTML embeds per-card JSON records with decks_cards.deck_quantity and decks_cards.deck_sideboard flags, which give an authoritative main/side split: maindeck sums to exactly 60 (34 spells + 26 lands), sideboard to exactly 15. Same list appears redundantly in the page's meta description and CreativeWork JSON-LD, and the two sources agree card-for-card. The maindeck list order above is spells-then-lands for readability; the source order started with lands.

BALANCE: every matchup was summed by hand rather than assumed. All seven balance (mirror 9-9, Temur Harmonizer 7-7, Izzet Lessons 9-9, Mono Red 5-5, Four-Color Rhythm 7-7, Jeskai Control 11-11, Bant Airbending 4-4). Additionally cross-checked that every OUT quantity is actually available in the 60 (e.g. OUT 4 Requiting Hex against a maindeck 4, OUT 3 Harvester against 3, OUT 2 Intimidation Tactics against 2) and every IN quantity is available in the 15 — no matchup overdraws either zone. Note Shoot the Sheriff comes in for 6 of 7 matchups and Quantum Riddler for 5 of 7, which is consistent but worth flagging as unusually uniform.

REASONING CAVEAT: the article does NOT write per-matchup sideboarding explanations. Each of the seven sections is just a heading, the word IN, a widget, the word OUT, a widget. The "reasoning" field therefore says "none given" first, then attaches the relevant sentence from the article's general Sideboard card-by-card commentary where one clearly applies. Do not treat those attached sentences as the author's stated per-matchup justification; they are mine to locate, his to have written about the card in general.

ONE POSSIBLE TYPO IN THE SOURCE (reported as-published, not corrected): the Temur Harmonizer OUT block cuts 2 Requiting Hex while the mirror and Jeskai cut all 4, and the Mono Red OUT cuts only 1 Bitter Triumph out of 3 — both are internally legal, just asymmetric. Reported verbatim.

=== VALIDATION PASS (independent, 2026-08-28) ===

VERDICT: zero corrections required. Nothing in the object was changed — no name rewritten, no quantity altered, no "balanced" flag flipped. The findings below are confirmations, not fixes.

1. CARD NAMES — all 25 distinct names verified individually against the Scryfall API (/cards/named?fuzzy=). All 25 resolved, and critically all 25 resolved to a name byte-identical to the submitted string, so fuzzy matching did no silent correcting: there was no shorthand to expand and no misspelling hiding behind a lenient match. Every one is legalities.standard == "legal" (Scryfall legality reflects the live ban list, so the 2026-08-10 bannings would have surfaced as "banned"). Resolved identity, mana cost, type, printing:
- Superior Spider-Man {2}{U}{B} Legendary Creature — Spider Human Hero (SPM)
- Harvester of Misery {3}{B}{B} Creature — Spirit (BIG)
- Deceit {4}{U/B}{U/B} Creature — Elemental Incarnation (ECL)
- Doomsday Excruciator {B}{B}{B}{B}{B}{B} Creature — Demon (DSK)
- Intimidation Tactics {B} Sorcery (DFT)
- Insatiable Avarice {B} Sorcery (OTJ)
- Winternight Stories {2}{U} Sorcery (TDM)
- Stock Up {2}{U} Sorcery (DFT)
- Deadly Cover-Up {3}{B}{B} Sorcery (MKM)
- Requiting Hex {B} Instant (ECL)
- Bitter Triumph {1}{B} Instant (TDC)
- Archenemy's Charm {B}{B}{B} Instant (EOE)
- Multiversal Passage Land (SPM)
- Gloomlake Verge Land (DSK)
- Undercity Sewers Land — Island Swamp (MKM)
- Restless Reef Land (LCI)
- Watery Grave Land — Island Swamp (TRK)
- Swamp Basic Land — Swamp (TRK)
- Quantum Riddler {3}{U}{U} Creature — Sphinx (EOE)
- Soul-Guide Lantern {1} Artifact (EOC)
- Torpor Orb {2} Artifact (BIG)
- Duress {B} Sorcery (FDN)
- Cruelclaw's Heist {B}{B} Sorcery (BLB)
- Shoot the Sheriff {1}{B} Instant (OTJ)
- Negate {1}{U} Instant (TMT)
Colour-identity plausibility check: every coloured card is mono-black, mono-blue, or Dimir (Deceit's hybrid {U/B} and Spider-Man's {2}{U}{B} both fit); the three colourless pieces (Multiversal Passage, Soul-Guide Lantern, Torpor Orb) are castable in any deck. Nothing off-colour, so nothing implausible for a Dimir Standard list. Two cards worth naming because they are the ones most likely to be doubted and both check out: Archenemy's Charm is a real EOE instant, not a confusion with Archfiend's or a Charm from another block; Torpor Orb is Standard-legal via its BIG (Big Score) printing rather than only the old New Phyrexia one.
Neither banned card appears anywhere in the 75 or in any IN/OUT block: no Badgermole Cub, no Stormchaser's Talent.
Three archetype cards listed in the task's reference set are genuinely absent from this build rather than dropped in extraction — no Day of Black Sun, Ghost Vacuum, Nowhere to Run, Cavern of Souls, Qarsi Revenant, Emeritus of Ideation, M.O.D.O.K., Hidden Lair, Strategic Betrayal, Flashfreeze, Deathmark, Annul, Outrageous Robbery, Wan Shi Tong Librarian, Malcolm Alluring Scoundrel, Preacher of the Schism, or Disdainful Stroke. That reference set is a superset of the archetype, not a checklist for this 75, so their absence is not a gap in the capture.

2. ARITHMETIC — recomputed from scratch with a script rather than trusting the submitted flags. IN/OUT totals: mirror 9/9, Temur Harmonizer 7/7, Izzet Lessons 9/9, Mono Red Aggro 5/5, Four-Color Rhythm 7/7, Jeskai Control 11/11, Bant Airbending 4/4. All seven balance, so all seven "balanced": true were already correct and none needed flipping. The submitted totals in the original notes match my independent sums exactly.

3. SIDEBOARD CONSISTENCY — the 15 parses as 3 Quantum Riddler + 2 Soul-Guide Lantern + 2 Torpor Orb + 4 Duress + 1 Cruelclaw's Heist + 2 Shoot the Sheriff + 1 Negate = 15 exactly. Every IN card across all seven matchups is present in that sideboard, and no IN quantity exceeds the copies owned (Duress 4/4, Quantum Riddler 3/3, Soul-Guide Lantern 2/2, Torpor Orb 2/2, Shoot the Sheriff 2/2, Cruelclaw's Heist 1/1, Negate 1/1 — the guide plays every sideboard slot to its full count in at least one matchup). Zero unmatched IN cards. Maindeck re-summed to 60 (34 spells + 26 lands: 2 Multiversal Passage, 4 Gloomlake Verge, 1 Undercity Sewers, 4 Restless Reef, 4 Watery Grave, 11 Swamp) and no OUT quantity exceeds the maindeck count (worst cases all exact: Requiting Hex 4/4, Harvester 3/3, Deceit 4/4, Intimidation Tactics 2/2, Deadly Cover-Up 2/2, Insatiable Avarice 3/3). 60 + 15 = 75.

RESIDUAL RISK, stated plainly: this pass validates that the names are real Standard-legal cards and that the numbers are internally consistent. It does NOT independently re-verify that these are the numbers Cardsrealm published — I did not re-fetch the article, so the extraction from data-name attributes and JSON-LD stands on the original capture. Internal consistency this tight (all seven matchups balancing, the sideboard exactly exhausted, main exactly 60) is decent circumstantial evidence the capture was faithful, since a garbled read would almost certainly break one of those constraints, but it is evidence and not proof. The two asymmetries flagged as possible source typos (Temur cutting 2 Requiting Hex rather than 4, Mono Red cutting 1 Bitter Triumph of 3) survive this pass unchanged: both are legal and both keep their matchup balanced, so there is no arithmetic ground to "correct" them, and correcting them would be substituting a guess for the published text.

matchups.reasoning: Duress is largely dead against a deck of creatures and lands rather than key noncreature spells. Preacher of the Schism is a resilient deathtouch blocker that generates card advantage and lifelink tokens; Shoot the Sheriff and M.O.D.O.K. handle their non-outlaw creature base, and M.O.D.O.K.'s -1/-1 static shrinks small dorks like Llanowar Elves. Keep Requiting Hex and Bitter Triumph to answer early creatures before landfall triggers snowball.

Mirror-adjacent matchup where the opponent runs planeswalkers like Kaito and noncreature spells like Nowhere to Run, making Negate valuable. Malcolm is a proactive flash flier that dodges sorcery-speed removal and draws cards in a grindy game. Day of Black Sun is weak because their real threats are resilient planeswalkers or higher-mana-value cards that dodge a low X, and they trim a Hidden Lair for a leaner, more proactive build.

They chain cheap spells to discount Hearth Elemental and Eddymurk Crab, so Negate stops payoffs like Prismari Charm or Traumatic Critique. Duress is weaker against a proactive, redundant spell-slinging plan. M.O.D.O.K.'s -1/-1 static shrinks their creatures, and removal like Bitter Triumph stays in for Hearth Elemental and Eddymurk Crab.

Against a reactive deck full of countermagic and sweepers, Negate stops card advantage engines like Stock Up and Consult the Star Charts or protects your threats from Three Steps Ahead. Malcolm is a resilient flash flying clock that is hard for them to interact with. Day of Black Sun is weak since their threats (Colorstorm Stallion, Champion of the Path) come down later, and trimming a land lowers the curve to play around counterspells.

An aggressive midrange deck of efficient creatures (Marauding Mako, Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodghast), so Preacher of the Schism's deathtouch and 4 toughness stabilize while drawing cards, and Shoot the Sheriff answers non-outlaw threats. Doomsday Excruciator is too slow at six mana and Winternight Stories does not affect the board when you need to trade with cheap creatures. Prioritize the removal suite to control their low curve.

Both decks fight over hand disruption and removal, so Negate protects your threats or stops their Strategic Betrayal and Deadly Cover-Up. Malcolm is a proactive flash clock that dodges sorcery-speed removal. Day of Black Sun is symmetrical and weak since both decks' top end (Doomsday Excruciator, M.O.D.O.K.) dodges low X values; trim a land to win the attrition war with a leaner build.

Negate answers key spells like Daydream and Practiced Offense while Malcolm gives a flash flier that trades well in the air against Sage of the Skies, Momo and Starfield Shepherd. Duress is weaker against a proactive, creature-heavy deck. Day of Black Sun is awkward because many of their threats have higher mana values that dodge a low X while a low X kills your own board; keep Requiting Hex for their many two-mana-or-less creatures.

A creature-based go-wide deck powered by Earthbender Ascension and Mightform Harmonizer, so Duress is largely dead once their board is rolling. Preacher of the Schism stabilizes against the swarm while drawing cards and M.O.D.O.K.'s -1/-1 static kills small creatures like Llanowar Elves and Poison Dart Frog. Keep the full removal suite to answer threats before landfall triggers snowball.

A fast creature-dense deck with hasty threats like Nova Hellkite, so Preacher of the Schism is a premium stabilizing blocker and M.O.D.O.K.'s -1/-1 static shrinks small aggressive creatures like Voice of Victory. Doomsday Excruciator at six mana is too slow and Stock Up does not affect the board when you must interact immediately. Keep the removal suite at full strength against their curve.

Full of efficient creatures like Gollum, Rhovanion Rampager and Bejeweled Warg, so Preacher of the Schism is a strong blocker and card advantage engine and Shoot the Sheriff picks off non-outlaw threats. Doomsday Excruciator is a big investment against efficient removal like Bitter Triumph and Assassin's Trophy, and Day of Black Sun is awkward against a curve topped by Professor Dellian Fel and Unholy Annex that dodges low X. Keep Requiting Hex and Bitter Triumph as core removal.

sources.notes:
VALIDATION PASS (2026-08-28). Result: zero corrections were needed. Every field below is unchanged from the input; the findings are appended.

=== CHECK 1: CARD NAMES ===
All 23 distinct names in the 75 were submitted to Scryfall's POST /cards/collection endpoint in one batch. not_found was empty: all 23 are real cards and all 23 report standard = "legal". No shorthand needed expanding, no name failed to resolve, no substitutions were made.
Printings: Swamp/Watery Grave (TRK), Superior Spider-Man (SPM), Deceit/Requiting Hex/Champion of the Path (ECL), Duress (FDN), Gloomlake Verge/Doomsday Excruciator (DSK), Restless Reef/Cavern of Souls/Preacher of the Schism/Malcolm (LCI), Bitter Triumph (TDC), Stock Up (DFT), Hidden Lair/M.O.D.O.K. (MSH), Day of Black Sun (TLA), Winternight Stories/Strategic Betrayal (TDM), Emeritus of Ideation (SOS), Deadly Cover-Up (MKM), Negate (TMT), Shoot the Sheriff (OTJ).
Scryfall-currency control: I checked the two cards the brief says were banned 2026-08-10. Scryfall returns Badgermole Cub = banned and Stormchaser's Talent = banned, so the legality data I read is current through the ban, not stale. Neither banned card appears anywhere in this 75.
Two naming details, neither an error:
- "Emeritus of Ideation" is the front face of a double-faced card whose full Scryfall name is "Emeritus of Ideation // Ancestral Recall" (layout "prepare", {3}{U}{U} // {U}, MV 5). Decklist convention is the front-face name, so I left it as published rather than expanding it.
- "Malcolm, Alluring Scoundrel" is correct as published; the reference list in the brief omitted the comma, the data did not.

=== CHECK 2: ARITHMETIC ===
Recomputed every IN and OUT sum programmatically rather than trusting the published "balanced" flags. All ten match: Mono Green Landfall 6/6, Selesnya Landfall 6/6, Izzet Spellementals 3/3, and the other seven 5/5. Every "balanced": true is therefore correct and none was flipped.
Deck totals recomputed by summing quantities: maindeck = 60 exactly, sideboard = 15 exactly.

=== CHECK 3: SIDEBOARD CONSISTENCY ===
Every IN card appears in the captured sideboard at a quantity greater than or equal to the amount brought in. No violations. Max demand per card across all plans: Preacher of the Schism 4 of 4, Malcolm 3 of 3, Negate 2 of 2, M.O.D.O.K. 1 of 1, Shoot the Sheriff 1 of 1. The three sideboard cards never brought in by any published plan are Strategic Betrayal, Deadly Cover-Up and Emeritus of Ideation, plus the 1 Doomsday Excruciator; that is the page's own gap, not an extraction error.
I also ran the reverse check, which the brief did not ask for: every OUT card exists in the maindeck at a sufficient quantity. All pass (e.g. Duress is cut 4, 3 and 2 across plans against a maindeck 4; Doomsday Excruciator cut 3 against a maindeck 3).

=== CORRECTION TO A CAVEAT IN THE PRIOR NOTES ===
The earlier extraction flagged as a discrepancy that "three plans cut Hidden Lair while the text says trim a land." That is not a discrepancy: Scryfall confirms Hidden Lair is a Land ({T}: Add {C}; {T}: Add {U} or {B} conditionally), so cutting it IS trimming a land and the prose matches. Likewise the Mono Green plan's Cavern of Souls cut is a land cut; the guide text simply does not mention it, which is incomplete prose on the page rather than bad data. I have dropped that caveat.

=== EXTRA: CARDS NAMED ONLY INSIDE THE REASONING TEXT ===
Not requested, but this is where fabricated names usually hide, so I verified all 32 of them against Scryfall too. Thirty resolved and are Standard-legal: Llanowar Elves, Nowhere to Run, Hearth Elemental (// Stoke Genius), Eddymurk Crab, Prismari Charm, Traumatic Critique, Consult the Star Charts, Three Steps Ahead, Colorstorm Stallion, Champion of the Path, Marauding Mako, Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodghast, Earthbender Ascension, Mightform Harmonizer, Poison Dart Frog, Nova Hellkite, Voice of Victory, Bejeweled Warg, Professor Dellian Fel, Unholy Annex (// Ritual Chamber), Assassin's Trophy, Ghost Vacuum, The End, Sheltered by Ghosts, Sage of the Skies, Starfield Shepherd, Daydream, Practiced Offense, Rhovanion Rampager, plus Kaito, Bane of Nightmares for the bare "Kaito".
Two are ambiguous short names rather than errors, and I left them as the page wrote them: "Momo" matches two Standard-legal cards (Momo, Friendly Flier and Momo, Playful Pet, both TLA), and "Gollum" matches three (Gollum, Riddle Master; Gollum, Silent Slinker; Gollum the Abandoned, all HOB). Nothing in the reasoning text is fabricated.
Also note the Golgari sentence "creatures like Gollum, Rhovanion Rampager and Bejeweled Warg" is a three-item list, not a single card named "Gollum, Rhovanion Rampager."

=== ROTATION WATCH (informational) ===
Six cards in the 75 come from sets old enough to be near rotation: Restless Reef, Cavern of Souls, Preacher of the Schism and Malcolm (all LCI, Nov 2023), Deadly Cover-Up (MKM, Feb 2024) and Shoot the Sheriff (OTJ, Apr 2024). They are legal today per Scryfall, but if this list is used after the fall 2026 rotation, recheck them.

=== CARRIED FORWARD FROM THE ORIGINAL EXTRACTION ===
Source method: page fetched with curl (HTTP 200, 112 KB); the 14 self.__next_f.push RSC chunks were reassembled and JSON-parsed, so all fields came from the embedded payload verbatim. The 75 came from the "mainboard"/"sideboard" arrays and the matchups from "initialGuides" (archetype_name, meta_percentage, cards_in, cards_out, guide_text).
Divergence from the original brief, still true: this is a live auto-updating page. There is no "UR Aggro" and no "Lifegain" matchup on it, and Jeskai Control is 7.9% rather than the brief's 13%. Percentages are the page's own one-decimal values. All ten matchups carry full guide_text, not just the top three; the "reasoning" fields are condensed paraphrases of that text, not quotations.
A separate "inverseGuides" array exists on the page (Jeskai Control, Selesnya Landfall, Golgari Midrange boarding AGAINST this deck, using Ghost Vacuum, The End, Sheltered by Ghosts). It is deliberately excluded here and must not be confused with this deck's own plans.
